strings.title: Groups of Negatives
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: A positive times a negative is that many groups of the negative, so the product is negative.
strings.keywords: groups of, repeated addition, jumps left, negative product
watchFor: Making the product positive (4 × −3 = 12): ask "Four groups of −3: are we gaining or owing?"
Adding instead of multiplying (4 × −3 = 1): ask "What does 4 × mean?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why is 4 × −3 negative?" Land: 4 × −3 is four jumps of −3 (four groups of debt), so the product is negative.

problems.notes: Look for: a known fact. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: numberline 0 +3x4
Look for: four groups of −3. Ask: "What changed from the last one?" Word choice: "Four groups of negative three." Model: numberline 0 -3x4

responses.tip: The target model.

responses.say: Four groups of three red tiles: 12 negatives.

responses.tip: Ask: four groups of −3: where do you end up, left or right of 0?

problems.notes: Look for: two jumps of −5. Ask: "Positive or negative? How do you know before calculating?" Model: numberline 0 -5x2
Look for: 6 × 4 = 24, negative. Ask: "Do you need to draw it?" Model: numberline 0 -4x6

responses.say: 6 × 4 is 24, and it's groups of a negative: −24.

responses.tip: Added. Ask: is that 6 groups of −4?

problems.notes: Look for: ten groups of −7. Ask: "How does × 10 work with negatives?" Model: text 10 x -7 = -70

responses.tip: Ask: ten groups of a debt of 7: do you owe or have?

problems.notes: Look for: half of 10 × −12. Ask: "Which strategy from multiplying whole numbers helps?" Model: text 10 x -12 = -120 ; 5 x -12 = -60

responses.tip: × 5 as half of × 10. Name it.

problems.notes: Look for: 25 × 4 = 100 (quarters), negative. Ask: "What do you know about 25 × 4?" Model: text 25 x 4 = 100 ; 25 x -4 = -100

responses.say: 4 quarters is a dollar, so 25 × 4 = 100. Negative: −100.

responses.tip: Added instead of multiplying. Ask: is that 25 groups of −4?

strings.title: Taking Away Groups
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: A negative times a number means taking away that many groups; add zero pairs first so there is something to take away.
strings.keywords: take away groups, zero pairs, opposite, negative times negative
watchFor: Thinking −3 × −2 is negative ("negatives make it negative"): build it with tiles and ask "What is left after we take away three groups of −2?"
Forgetting to add zero pairs: ask "There's nothing on the mat. How can we take away?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why does taking away negatives leave positives?" Land: −3 × −2 means take away three groups of −2; after adding zero pairs and removing the negatives, six positives are left.

problems.notes: Look for: a known fact. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: tiles 3 x 2
Look for: take away three groups of 2. Ask: "What could −3 groups mean?" Word choice: "Take away three groups of 2." Model: tiles -3 x 2

responses.say: Add 6 zero pairs, take away three groups of 2 positives: 6 negatives left.
responses.tip: The target model. Ask: why add zero pairs?

problems.notes: Look for: take away three groups of −2. Ask: "What's left this time?" Model: tiles -3 x -2

responses.say: Add 6 zero pairs, take away three groups of −2: 6 positives left.
It's the opposite of 3 × −2, which is −6.
responses.tip: The opposite of the opposite. Name it.
Ask: after taking away the negatives, which tiles are left?

problems.notes: Look for: the opposite of 4 × −5. Ask: "Can you predict the sign first?" Model: tiles -4 x -5

responses.say: Take away four groups of −5: 20 positives left.

responses.tip: Ask: what's the opposite of 4 × −5?

problems.notes: Look for: take away two groups of 7. Ask: "Positive or negative?" Model: tiles -2 x 7
Look for: opposite of 6 × −6. Ask: "Do you need the tiles now?" Model: text 6 x -6 = -36 ; -6 x -6 = 36

responses.tip: Ask: taking away groups of negatives leaves what?

problems.notes: Look for: opposite of 10 × −9. Ask: "What's the sign rule you're noticing?" Model: text 10 x -9 = -90 ; -10 x -9 = 90

strings.title: The Pattern of Products
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Following a pattern: as one factor goes down by 1, the product changes by the other factor, even past zero.
strings.keywords: pattern, decrease by, sign, continue the pattern
watchFor: Stopping at 0 × −4: ask "What comes next in the pattern?"
Continuing the pattern the wrong way (−1 × −4 = −4): ask "What has been happening to the product each time?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did the pattern show −1 × −4 = 4?" Land: each step down in the first factor adds 4 to the product, so after 0 the products become positive.

problems.notes: Look for: three groups of −4. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: numberline 0 -4x3
Look for: −8. Ask: "How did the product change?" Model: text 3 x -4 = -12 ; 2 x -4 = -8

responses.tip: Ask: why up by 4?

problems.notes: Look for: up by 4 again. Ask: "What's the pattern?" Model: text 3 x -4 = -12 ; 2 x -4 = -8 ; 1 x -4 = -4

responses.say: −4. Each time the product goes up 4.

problems.notes: Look for: zero groups is 0, and it fits the pattern. Ask: "Does the pattern agree?" Model: text 1 x -4 = -4 ; 0 x -4 = 0

responses.say: Zero groups of anything is 0. And −4 + 4 = 0.

problems.notes: Look for: continue the pattern: up 4 again. Ask: "What must come next?" Word choice: "The pattern says it goes up by 4 each time." Model: text 0 x -4 = 0 ; -1 x -4 = 4

responses.say: The product keeps going up by 4: 4.
responses.tip: The target reasoning.

responses.say: Take away one group of −4: 4 positives left.
responses.tip: Connects to Taking Away Groups.
Ask: what's been happening to the product each step?

problems.notes: Look for: 8. Ask: "Does the pattern keep going?" Model: text -1 x -4 = 4 ; -2 x -4 = 8
Look for: jump ahead in the pattern. Ask: "Can you skip to it?" Model: text -5 x -4 = 20

responses.tip: Ask: what does the pattern say happens past 0?

strings.title: Dividing Integers
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Use the related multiplication fact: −12 ÷ 3 = −4 because 3 × −4 = −12; the sign follows the same rules.
strings.keywords: related facts, fact family, inverse, quotient, sign
watchFor: Getting the size right but the sign wrong: ask "What times 3 makes −12?"
Reversing dividend and divisor: ask "Which number is being shared or grouped?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did multiplication help you divide?" Land: every division has a related multiplication; the same sign rules apply: same signs give a positive, different signs a negative.

problems.notes: Look for: three groups of −4. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: numberline 0 -4x3
Look for: 3 × −4 = −12, so −4. Ask: "How does the last problem help?" Word choice: "−12 shared into 3 equal groups." Model: numberline 0 -4x3

responses.tip: The target strategy.

responses.say: Split −12 into 3 equal jumps: each is −4.

responses.tip: Ask: 3 times 4 is 12, not −12. What times 3 is −12?

problems.notes: Look for: how many groups of −4 in −12? Ask: "Same fact family?" Model: numberline 0 -4x3

responses.tip: Ask: −4 × −3 is what? Is it −12?

problems.notes: Look for: −5 × −4 = 20. Ask: "What times −5 gives 20?" Model: text -5 x -4 = 20 ; 20 / -5 = -4

responses.tip: Ask: −5 × 4 is what?

problems.notes: Look for: −9 × 4 = −36. Ask: "Positive or negative? Why?" Model: text -9 x 4 = -36 ; -36 / -9 = 4

responses.tip: Ask: −9 × −4 is what?

problems.notes: Look for: 25 × −4 = −100. Ask: "Which fact do you know?" Model: text 25 x -4 = -100 ; -100 / 25 = -4
Look for: 7 × 12 = 84, same signs. Ask: "How do you know the sign first?" Model: text -7 x 12 = -84 ; -84 / -7 = 12

responses.tip: Split the dividend. Nice.
